findings.title: Object and array escape tracking stops before contained references and non-CallExpression invocations
findings.contract: Latest admission: aliases, indirect/computed mutation and escape to unmodeled calls invalidate array/config inference.
findings.rootCause: mutationOrigin returns the outer array/object identity without traversing contained references; SpreadElement is not resolved. Escape discovery handles only CallExpression, skipping tagged-template and constructor arguments. Local parameter mutation cannot reconnect to the passed object.
findings.observableConsequence: Six concrete sources mutate a config text or loop table into billing_items, yet the exact public CLI reports PASS with no findings by retaining the original SELECT/quota value.
findings.recommendedNextAction: Invalidate contained config/array identities on unmodeled escapes through aggregate values, spreads, tags and constructors; avoid treating retained initializer provenance as immutable. Add paired public CLI cases.

findings.title: Destructuring assignment leaves do not invalidate the object actually written
findings.contract: Latest admission: const does not make objects immutable; indirect/computed mutation invalidates config and finite-table inference.
findings.rootCause: For assignment-pattern LHS, mutationOrigin identifies the object/array pattern itself. It does not inspect assignment leaves such as c.text or tables[0]. The referenced config or array remains untainted.
findings.observableConsequence: Object-pattern and array-pattern assignments visibly set DELETE FROM billing_items or replace the quota loop entry with billing_items; all three CLI probes return PASS.
findings.recommendedNextAction: Walk destructuring assignment destinations and invalidate their real origin symbols/objects before SQL inference. Preserve harmless destructuring reads.

findings.title: Read method names are trusted without verifying the callable identity
findings.contract: Latest admission: effective static members preserve effects and mutable configs require conservative provenance; local function names alone do not establish effect/purity.
findings.rootCause: readMethods exemptions depend only on member spelling (join, slice, etc.). A locally declared impure method with this.text assignment is treated as an intrinsic read method. mutationOrigin does not resolve ThisKeyword to the receiver.
findings.observableConsequence: Calling a config own join/slice method changes its text to DELETE FROM billing_items; the later client.query(config) is inferred as SELECT 1 and returns PASS. Alias receiver variant also passes.
findings.recommendedNextAction: Base read exemptions on verified builtin receiver/callable provenance, or invalidate unknown/impure receiver methods, including local methods using this.

findings.title: Known node-fetch effect is lost at namespace.default
findings.contract: Latest admission: imports, destructuring and static object members preserve known host effects; lexical aliases remain detectable.
findings.rootCause: node-fetch import resolves to the fetch marker, but memberEffect propagates module effects only for axios/got/undici. A literal default property on the node-fetch namespace resolves to null. Aliasing and destructuring that member retain the omission.
findings.observableConsequence: The CLI accepts import * as nf from node-fetch; nf.default(url), namespace default alias/destructure, and await-import default invocation. The paired default import from the same module is correctly flagged direct_fetch.
findings.recommendedNextAction: Preserve the namespace/default-export shape for the already recognized node-fetch module through static aliases and destructuring; keep local inert default methods benign.

findings.title: query.bind construction is classified as a SQL execution
findings.contract: Actual known host effects versus inert local operations; binding constructs a callable, as the source itself documents.
findings.rootCause: visit skips bind for network effects but does not skip bind when name is query. It interprets the thisArg as SQL; the later invocation also discards bound SQL arguments.
findings.observableConsequence: An unused const q=client.query.bind(client,"SELECT 1") returns FAIL/unresolved_query_expression even though no query occurs. A bound function called only with SELECT 1 also fails. Unused fetch.bind and pure local query.bind are accepted.

findings.title: Exact forwarder admission also accepts default and rest parameter transformations
findings.confidence: high for admission mismatch; no demonstrated executed domain bypass
findings.contract: Existing forwarder may be recognized only as the exact preexisting direct client.query(text, values), with its own unchanged parameters; no additional transformation.
findings.rootCause: transparentForwarder checks identifier names and argument count, but not parameter initializer or dotDotDotToken. It discloses transformed declarations as existing-transparent-parameter-forwarder.
findings.observableConsequence: An arrow with text="DELETE FROM billing_items" defaults or ...values receives PASS and the exact-forwarder disclosure. Default/rest alter caller-to-client behavior. Exact body and same-file consumer controls still work; no default-triggered execution was run or claimed.
